items.title: Bill Kirchner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2021
items.q: So I had a repairman, Perry Ritter, who is a great repairman, he rebuilt the horn with alternate keys so I could still play.

ctx.x: Yeah, thank you for those answers. Has your melody conception changed over the years? You lost the use of your right arm and the fact that you managed to keep playing but in a different way, did it affect the way you think about melodies?

Yeah. Well I had my soprano, after I had my — I had surgery in 1993 that left my — to remove a spinal tumor that was life-threatening so that left my right hand basically crippled. I mean I have only a very limited use of my right hand so the only horn I could still play of the nine saxophones and flutes and clarinets I’ve played at one point, the only one I could still play was soprano saxophone. So I had a repairman, Perry Ritter, who is a great repairman, he rebuilt the horn with alternate keys so I could…

staggered at how long the tracks were. And I’d like to think that they’re not boring or not going on past their bedtime. But they’re really extended and it’s just the two of us. So I mean you learn to pace yourself in a different way.
